_framework_note: ATI's 10-K narrative does NOT name specific Pentagon Program Elements / PE numbers / programs-of-record. Defense end-markets are described only at the generic platform level ('naval nuclear products, military jet engines, fixed wing and rotorcraft products, armor applications'). This is the OPPOSITE of the YSS/IONQ short-thesis pattern (which depended on small-cap loading forward narrative on a single named, vanishing PE). The J-Book divergence framework therefore has limited bite here — no single named program can fail; risk is diffused across the megacap-prime supply chain. The pentagon_jbook queries below are run against IMPLIED programs (F-35, F-22A, F-15EX, B-21, CV-22, KC-46A, Hypersonics, Columbia, Virginia) that PLAUSIBLY consume ATI titanium/nickel, but the claims do NOT explicitly cite these. Severity reflects this looseness: even an UNFUNDED-status implied program scores at most MODERATE, because the claim binding to that program is weak.

supports: usaspending.query_dod_contracts: 'ATI Inc' returned 36 awards / $8.1M total, but the top-listed hits are 'GBI Cincinnati Inc' and 'Cincinnati Incorporated' (machine-tool false positives, NOT ATI Inc the materials company)
'ATI Specialty Materials' = 0 awards
'ATI Forged Products' = 0 awards
'ATI Titanium' = 0 awards
'Allegheny Technologies' = 1 award worth $1.44M (Allegheny Ludlum LLC, 6Al-4V titanium, contract W15QKN08C0452)
scores.M_value: Direct DoD prime contracts to ATI/Allegheny entities are de minimis (<$2M aggregate across 2018-2024) once false-positive Cincinnati matches are excluded.
scores.interpretation: The +80% titanium capacity expansion is being justified to investors partly on 'A&D demand growth.' Direct DoD obligations to ATI entities are negligible — confirming ATI is a sub-tier supplier to primes (Boeing, LMT, RTX/Pratt, GE Aerospace), not a direct DoD prime. The risk: if commercial-aerospace build rates (Boeing 737 MAX, 787; Airbus A320neo; LEAP/GTF engine ramps) slip — which is the actual driver of ~60% of HPMC revenue — the capacity could be stranded. The DEFENSE part of the capacity story is thin and unverifiable through usaspending. Score MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY on the implicit 'defense demand justifies capacity' framing — defense is not where the demand is provable; commercial-aerospace cyclicality is the real exposure (not in scope of this J-Book cohort).

summary: ATI on the J-Book cohort: the framework PROBES correctly (pentagon_jbook fires on every J-Book-grounded claim) but the SUBJECT is mis-matched to this pattern. ATI doesn't name PEs; its forward defense narrative is too diffuse for the J-Book divergence test to land. All named-platform proxies the framework can check (F-35, B-21, CV-22, KC-46A, Hypersonics Prototyping) are FUNDED_STEADY. The only signal of any concern is the implicit defense-demand framing of the +80% titanium capacity buildout (C5) — and that risk is more about commercial-aerospace build-rate cyclicality (out of cohort scope) than DoD program risk. NET: no Signal-OS short signal triggered by the J-Book cohort on ATI at the 2024-09-01 cutoff.
